The court made a first-instance judgment on a dispute over liability for sexual harassment damages, finding that the existing evidence was insufficient to confirm that the defendant had committed sexual harassment, and rejected the plaintiff's application.
The university involved issued a briefing, expressing respect for judicial decisions and launching an investigation and review of previous disciplinary actions and related academic integrity issues.
Large social platforms issued management announcements to permanently ban accounts that pretend to be relevant identities and spread false information.

The plaintiff released self-defense materials on social media in response to the dispute over thesis and evidence collection, which was regarded by public opinion as further intensifying the confrontation.

According to public information, the doctoral admission/proposed admission status of the overseas university where the plaintiff plans to enroll has changed, which has triggered widespread concern and follow-up complaints.
The plaintiff filed an appeal and was accepted by the court of second instance, and the case entered the second instance procedure.
The dissertation involved was removed from the academic resource platform, and the retraction mechanism and promoters triggered new disputes over procedures and credibility.
The second-instance judgment rendered and upheld the first-instance conclusion, dismissed the appeal, and the relevant civil disputes were concluded in the second-instance procedure.

The court released the second-instance judgment information through official channels. The results of the second-instance were intensively known to the public and triggered subsequent public opinion and pressure for disposal.
